rule: Biomechanics, anatomy and numerical deformation evidence do not prove exterior human appearance. Every body region must also have real-human visual surface evidence through the relevant motion states before whole-body visual validation can close.
source_rules: Prefer real-human video or sequential photography that exposes the relevant surface landmarks.
Use multiple subjects/body builds where practical; one person's fold depth or muscle contour is not universal.
Use multiple camera angles when the anatomical transition cannot be established from one view.
Clothing, sensors or straps may limit a source to gross silhouette/motion conclusions; record that uncertainty.
External visuals are observation-only development evidence and never production content, copied geometry, texture or identity.

exit_rule: Stage 4 visual-evidence closure is blocked while any region is missing the real-human surface states/views needed for its coupling and movement families. A region may remain partial when source limitations are explicitly recorded, but Critical/High visual claims cannot be closed from anatomy/kinematics alone.

summary.interpretation: partial means some real-human visual motion/surface evidence exists; it is not sufficient for final exterior skin/muscle acceptance.
